reason: Headlamps, rear lamps, and number-plate lamps must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and when visibility is less than 150 meters.
Do not pass other traffic when approaching the summit of a rise, a curve, or anywhere visibility is too restricted to see oncoming traffic.
Do not cross or enter a public road unless it is clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance, or you can do so with safety.
After an accident, a driver must immediately stop, check for and assist with injuries, and not consume alcohol before reporting.
A traffic signal alternately directs traffic to stop and permits it to proceed, but flashing red is not explicitly covered.
At a junction where vehicles move around a traffic island, give way to all traffic approaching from your right.
A driver must immediately give way to any emergency vehicle sounding a siren and displaying warning lights.
Before stopping or turning, give a clear, timely signal of your intention.
Towing at over 30 km/h with a rope or chain is not allowed, and a towed vehicle may only carry passengers at over 30 km/h if it is a semi-trailer.

Rear seatbelts must be worn if fitted, seatbelts are not compulsory when reversing, children are defined as 3-14 unless taller than 1.5m, and an adult may not occupy a seat without a seatbelt if a belted seat is available.
A Code 2 learner's licence authorises driving only under the direct supervision of a licensed driver for that class.
A light motor vehicle's tyres must have a tread pattern at least 1mm deep.
